turns.prompt_text: search for people with two rows of teeth
turns.response_html: Two rows of teeth, often called "shark teeth," usually happen in children when permanent teeth grow in behind baby teeth that haven't fallen out yet; the medical term for having extra teeth is hyperdontia, which can also affect adults.

turns.prompt_text: find some more information on hyperdontia
turns.response_html:
Hyperdontia, the condition of having extra teeth (supernumerary teeth), is often linked to genetic factors or certain syndromes like Gardner's or Ehlers-Danlos.

Symptoms often involve:

  • Visible extra teeth
  • Crowding or misalignment of other teeth
  • Delayed eruption of permanent teeth
  • Sometimes pain or discomfort

Treatment often involves extracting the extra teeth, especially if they cause oral health issues like overcrowding or affect the proper eruption of permanent teeth. However, if the extra teeth cause no problems, a dentist may simply monitor them.

Would you like to know more about the types of supernumerary teeth?

turns.prompt_text: is there a company that has developed some way to grow an extra row of teeth
turns.response_html: A Japanese biotech company called Toregem Biopharma is developing a drug to stimulate the growth of a third set of teeth by blocking the protein USAG-1, which naturally suppresses tooth growth. Their goal is for this tooth regeneration medicine to be available by 2030, offering an alternative to implants and dentures for people with missing teeth.

turns.prompt_text: other people in India who have multiple rows of teeth
turns.response_html:
Yes, there have been notable cases of extreme hyperdontia in India.

  • Kalpana Balan (from India) holds the Guinness World Record for the most teeth in a female's mouth, with 38 teeth (six more than average).
  • In 2019, surgeons in Chennai removed 526 tooth-like structures from the jaw of a seven-year-old boy.
  • In 2014, a 17-year-old boy named Ashik Gavai had 232 teeth removed in a surgery in Mumbai.

turns.prompt_text: hey Google did the Buddha say anything about having extra teeth
turns.response_html: The Buddha did not speak about having extra teeth, but having forty teeth is listed as one of the 32 Major Marks of a Great Man that the historical Buddha possessed. This is interpreted as a sign of perfection, achieved through a life of truthful speech and avoiding malicious gossip.

turns.prompt_text: hey Google how many teeth does a normal person have
turns.response_html: A normal adult human has 32 permanent teeth, which includes 4 wisdom teeth. If the wisdom teeth are removed, the count is typically 28.

turns.prompt_text: hey Google tell me more information about having 40 teeth in one of the 32 marks of a great man
turns.response_html:
The mark of 40 teeth symbolizes the perfection and purity of the Buddha's speech, and is often linked to the wholesome karma of avoiding divisive language and working to foster unity and harmony among all beings over countless lifetimes.

These teeth are also described as being even, close together (gapless), perfectly white, and a feature that distinguishes a Great Man from ordinary people, who typically have 32 teeth.

turns.prompt_text: hey Google what are the 32 marks of a great man
turns.response_html:
The 32 marks of a Great Man (or Mahāpuruṣa Lakṣaṇa) are a traditional set of auspicious physical characteristics, most famously attributed to a Buddha or a universal monarch.

They include features such as:

  • Wheels on the soles of the feet.
  • A protuberance on the crown of the head (Uṣṇīṣa).
  • Skin of a golden hue.
  • Forty teeth that are white and even.
  • A tuft of white hair between the eyebrows (Ūrṇā).
  • A lion-shaped torso and jaw.
  • Hands that can reach down to the knees while standing.

Buddhist tradition teaches that each mark is the result of accumulating immense positive karma and performing specific ethical actions over countless lifetimes.
